report.summary: Alert EVAL-04 on host SRV-FS-02 represents active ransomware precursor activity. Within a span of two minutes, PsExec spawned a command shell, volume shadow copies were deleted, system recovery was disabled, the Security event log was cleared, and Microsoft Defender real-time monitoring was disabled. Threat intelligence confirms past true-positive alerts for these indicators.

claims.text: The alerting tool EDR reported multiple defense and recovery commands executed on host SRV-FS-02 (unverified by us).
PsExec (PSEXESVC.exe) spawned cmd.exe as user CORP\adm-temp on SRV-FS-02.
vssadmin.exe was used to delete volume shadow copies via the command 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet'.
wevtutil.exe was used to clear Windows security event logs via the command 'wevtutil cl Security'.
PowerShell was used to disable Microsoft Defender real-time monitoring via 'Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true'.
bcdedit.exe was executed via the command shell to disable system recovery via 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No'.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host SRV-FS-02 from the network immediately to prevent potential ransomware deployment or lateral movement.
Disable or reset credentials for the compromised user account CORP\adm-temp.
Collect memory and disk forensics from SRV-FS-02 for detailed analysis.
Hunt across the enterprise for similar PsExec executions and defense-evasion command lines.
Tune detection rules for rapid shadow copy deletion and event log clearing patterns.
